conventions.convention: Throughout the assigned affine construction, n ≥ 2, R₀ = Z[Q,Q⁻¹], Λ = Zⁿ, and A = R₀[X₁±¹,…,Xₙ±¹]; adjacent transpositions interchange the corresponding Laurent variables.
Dᵢ(f) = (f − sᵢ(f))/(1 − Xᵢ/Xᵢ₊₁), so Dᵢ(Xᵢ) = −Xᵢ₊₁ and Dᵢ(Xᵢ₊₁) = Xᵢ₊₁.
The multiplicative normalization is (Tᵢ − Q)(Tᵢ + 1) = 0 and Tᵢf − sᵢ(f)Tᵢ = (Q − 1)Dᵢ(f). In particular TᵢXᵢTᵢ = QXᵢ₊₁; comparison with symmetric normalization uses Q = v² and Tᵢ = vUᵢ.
Skew multiplication is (a[w])(b[v]) = a w(b)[wv]. The skew group algebra has underlying K-vector space with basis [w], but its stated central coefficient algebra is R₀.
The center equality is asserted over the universal ring R₀ only; no assertion that centers commute with arbitrary specialization is included.

load_bearing.statement: For n ≥ 2, the coefficient map A → Hₙᵃᶠᶠ is injective and {X^λ T_w : λ ∈ Zⁿ, w ∈ Sₙ} is an R₀-basis. For every commutative R₀-algebra R′, scalar extension has the tensor-image basis and is the affine presentation with its relations mapped to R′.

The elements 𝒯ᵢ = Q[sᵢ] + (Q − 1)([1] − [sᵢ])/(1 − Xᵢ/Xᵢ₊₁) preserve A, satisfy the quadratic and braid relations, and obey 𝒯ᵢf − sᵢ(f)𝒯ᵢ = (Q − 1)Dᵢ(f). They define an R₀-algebra homomorphism from the affine presentation to K ⋊ Sₙ, and their [sᵢ] coefficients are nonzero in K.

For n ≥ 2, the reduced products T_w are well-defined and form an R₀-basis of the finite type-A algebra with quadratic relation (Tᵢ − Q)(Tᵢ + 1) = 0; their tensor images remain a basis after every commutative R₀-algebra extension.
For n ≥ 2, A = Z[Q,Q⁻¹][X₁±¹,…,Xₙ±¹] is a domain with Laurent monomial basis. Dᵢ(f) = (f − sᵢ(f))/(1 − Xᵢ/Xᵢ₊₁) lies uniquely in A and satisfies Dᵢ(fg) = Dᵢ(f)g + sᵢ(f)Dᵢ(g).
Over the universal coefficient ring R₀, Z(Hₙᵃᶠᶠ) = A^{Sₙ}.

published_dependencies.used_for: Existence and universal properties of the finite and affine presentations, and finite generator-word expansions.
Base change of relation quotients and transport of explicit free bases without a flatness assumption.
Laurent monomial bases, domain and fraction-field constructions, and the even/odd decomposition Z[v,v⁻¹] = R₀ ⊕ vR₀.
The type-A Coxeter identification with Sₙ and the length conventions used in reduced products.
Independence of finite Hecke products from the chosen reduced expression.
The generic parameter ring, odd-component parameter convention, and symmetric quadratic normalization underlying the finite-basis supplier.
Reduced products and spanning used by the generic standard-basis supplier.
The commuting length-operator representation underlying the published generic standard-basis proof; its six commutation configurations were inspected.
The finite standard basis over Z[v,v⁻¹] and its arbitrary commutative base change before multiplicative-normalization descent.
The conversion Tᵢ = vUᵢ, Q = v² and preservation of equal-length braid relations.
Absence of zero divisors in Z in the Laurent-domain verification.
Nontriviality of Z in the Laurent-domain verification.
The domain convention includes commutativity, 1 ≠ 0, and absence of zero divisors.

concerns.concern: The second prose paragraph says the proof chain “derives the $A$-basis $\{X^\lambda T_w\}$.” This family is an R₀-basis, as the theorem correctly states, and is not A-linearly independent: its members 1 and X₁ already satisfy X₁·1 − 1·X₁ = 0 with nonzero coefficients in A. The A-basis is {T_w}. The item theorem and proof give the correct coefficient rings; the page claim as written is false.

seams_checked.note: Checked the compact affine presentation against the Bernstein definition and its proved equivalence, including the sign of the polynomial divided difference. The Jucys–Murphy lemma F3 and straightening lemma F4 faithfully use the finite multiplicative basis and arbitrary coefficient extension; the n = 1 spanning case is handled separately. The supplier page makes no converse dependence on cyclotomic results.

The component-shift lemma F6 cites exactly TᵢXᵢTᵢ = QXᵢ₊₁ and TᵢX₁ = X₁Tᵢ for i ≥ 2; its use to commute T_c₀ past X₁ agrees with the supplier. The page retains the same multiplicative normalization without square-root rescaling. The affine suppliers do not rely on the later Murphy construction.
